note: Wave 3: hardware H.264 (then HEVC) DECODE. Written by opus-vdec from gpu/hwcodec/facts/VDEC_PROTOCOL.md (read it first: sections 0, 4, 5, 7). Rules: gpu/hwcodec/WORKER_RULES.md (owned files, /tmp/n2hw-<id>, no phone, no vendor code in the tree). Order: DEC01 + DEC07 + DEC08 start at once; DEC02 after DEC01 reaches VD-c; DEC03 after DEC02's first trace; DEC04 after DEC07's ABI text is accepted; DEC05 then DEC06. None of this needs the phone until DEC03 passes and the kernel window fix is in an image.
achievable_today: DEC01 to VD-c/VD-d on the fake (hours, if the get_ringbuf cause is a shim/AP hand-over detail)
not_achievable_today: a decoded picture on the PC (the fake can never produce pixels; at best header parsing via DEC03)
any phone decode (needs the window fix in an image, VENC phone cycles first)
the VT decoder plug-in end to end

packages.title: AP-side H.264/HEVC decode client (n2ap_vdec) for the host runner: the user-space vdec_common_if.c + vdec_vcu_if.c + decoder LOCK/UNLOCK power role
deliverable: n2ap_vdec_query_cap / open (INIT, IPI_VDEC_H264=2 or H265=3, QUERY_CAP on IPI_VDEC_COMMON=1) / set_param / decode(bs handle, fb handles or none) / flush (RESET) / close (DEINIT), mirroring vdec_common_if.c; vsi via n2vcu_map_dm_addr; ACK-then-dispatched ordering exactly as V41 rev 3.

FIRST: make AP_IPIMSG_DEC_START pass the vendor's input import. Today it answers status -1 with '[ERROR] get_ringbuf input handle NULL !!' (libvpud_vcodec.so get_ringbuf @0x8c70). Trace the host calls ion_import/ion_mmap/ion_share/ion_free during START (n2a32_trace_hostcall or a shim-side log in your own test build), read the callers around libvpud_vcodec.so 0xae86..0xb2c0 (addresses/literals only, no listing > 20 lines in the tree), compare with the kernel (get_mapped_fd for bs, each fb plane and general_buf: vdec_vcu_if.c:72-158, vdec_common_if.c:217-260). If the fix needs a V34 shim change, post the exact patch to hw-v34/hw-iv; do not edit shim/.

Handle VCU->AP requests: LOCK/UNLOCK_CORE (RWVC_BLK_VDEC_CORE + its parent VDEC_SOC) and LOCK/UNLOCK_LAT (VDEC_SOC) as power refs; racing words (68 x u32 at VDEC_RACING+0x100) restored on first lock, saved on last unlock; HW-break sequence of mtk_vcodec_dec_pm.c:296-460 before the last unlock; WAITISR: status 0 -> RWVC_IRQ_VDEC, 1 -> RWVC_IRQ_VDEC_LAT, 500 ms, result written back into status; GET_FRAME_BUFFER blocks up to 1 s on the client's free-fb queue and fills vsi.dec (fb_va cookie, index, fb_dma[], fb_fd[] share ids, general_buf); PUT_FRAME_BUFFER harvests list_disp/list_free into the client's output queue (cookie, poc, timestamp).
n2vc_dma_sync around each START: bitstream to_device before, every output plane from_device after it appears in list_disp.

A runner hook for the host: a small CLI /tmp build (not in the tree's host/ dir) or a test that starts n2vhost and decodes tests/vectors (generate with ffmpeg at test time: testsrc 320x240 and 1920x1080, -pix_fmt yuv420p, libx264 main, -bf 0 and -bf 2, and libx265) up to the first unmet hardware need, printing the milestone: VD-a QUERY_CAP, VD-b INIT, VD-c START accepted (no get_ringbuf error), VD-d first VDEC register access, VD-e first WAITISR.
packages.host_test_oracle: Message layouts checked against the kernel header compiled 32- and 64-bit (as V41's probe_kernel.c); on the fake: QUERY_CAP lists H264/H265 and NV12 (literal list in gpu/hwcodec/facts/VDEC_PROTOCOL.md 2.4), INIT returns a vsi inside the DMEM, START no longer logs get_ringbuf (vendor log captured through n2shim_log), milestone VD-d reached or the first unmet need named.

packages.title: VLD barrel-shifter + AVC_VLD syntax model in the fake hardware so the vendor can parse SPS/PPS/slice headers on the PC
owned_files: gpu/hwcodec/tests/hw/vdec/** (new files, linked into the fake through a hook T02 accepts)
depends_on: post the hook signature to hw-t02 (owner of n2vc_hw_fake.c) before coding
deliverable: Model, inferred from the vendor's own use (H264_HAL_ShiftGetBitStream @0xfd186 -> vdec_hal_read_vld(hw,core,n); H264_HAL_UeCodeNum @0xfd218 -> read AVC_VLD reg 0x8f; vdec_hal_set_vld_vfifo, vdec_hal_init_barrel_shift, H264_HAL_InitH264BarrelShifter @0xffd18, vdec_hal_read_vld_rptr): vfifo start/end + read pointer from the registers the vendor writes, reading VLD reg n shifts n bits and returns the next 32 bits big-endian, AVC_VLD 0x8f returns ue(v), the se(v) and emulation-prevention behaviour determined from the trace. Every register meaning documented [V] (vendor use + test) or [I].
Same for LAT_VLD / LAT_AVC_VLD if the trace shows the LAT core parsing; HEVC (HEVC_VLD) only if H265_parse* read registers.

packages.title: vcodecd decoder service + client library (decode protocol next to the encoder's)
owned_files: proposed protocol text for include/n2vcd_proto.h posted to hw-lead (frozen header)
deliverable: Protocol: DEC_OPEN(codec, w, h, out format NV12|MM21) -> caps + buffer sizes; DEC_INPUT(bitstream in a shared RWVC buffer, pts) ; FRAME_OUT(handle, pts, crop, poc) ; DEC_RELEASE(handle) ; FLUSH ; CLOSE. Output buffers are RWVC_DMA_SHARED client buffers (RWVC_DMA_INFO for the pa). Session limits and fatal-guest handling exactly as IP's encoder path (exit 70).
Client: n2vcd_dec_* with timeouts, used by DEC06.
packages.host_test_oracle: End-to-end on the fake: open/input/flush/close with the fake answering through DEC03's model; error paths (daemon gone, bad sizes, too many buffers) return documented codes.

packages.title: VideoToolbox decoder plug-in Slim.videodecoder (SLIMRegister): avc1/hvc1 hardware decoder object over DEC05
depends_on: DEC08 ABI facts (decoder class record) before any slot is filled
deliverable: Object: CMBaseObject of VTVideoDecoderGetClassID(); class record slots per DEC08 (StartSession, DecodeFrame, CopySupportedPropertyDictionary, SetProperties, CopySerializableProperties, CanAcceptFormatDescription, FinishDelayedFrames ...); avcC/hvcC parsing from the CMFormatDescription extensions into Annex-B parameter sets for the daemon; length-prefixed NALs -> SET_PARAM_NAL_SIZE_LENGTH or Annex-B conversion; output CVPixelBuffer NV12 (420v/420f per full_range) from VTDecoderSessionGetPixelBufferPool / SetPixelBufferAttributes, copy (and MM21 detile if needed) from the DMA buffer, crop/clean aperture, emit with VTDecoderSessionEmitDecodedFrame in decode order with pts; flush on FinishDelayedFrames.

Registration: VTRegisterVideoDecoderWithInfo('avc1'/'hvc1'), IsHardwareAccelerated true, gated by a switch file exactly like P04's encoder gate (do not offer it unless the daemon works); software fallback = return an error that makes VT pick Apple's H264SW/VCPHEVC [I: verify the retry behaviour as P04 noted for encoders].
